title: Regular Expressions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Regular Expressions”?
options: Basic and extended regular expressions in external tools
questions.answer_key: Basic and extended regular expressions in external tools
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Basic and extended regular expressions in external tools” under lesson 92, “Regular Expressions”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Regular Expressions”?
options: Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Preserve pathnames as data and test file workflows in a disposable directory.
questions.answer_key: Preserve pathnames as data and test file workflows in a disposable directory.
questions.explanation: Preserve pathnames as data and test file workflows in a disposable directory. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Regular Expressions”?
options: Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
